newsitem.title: USA: FTC member eyes privacy issues in online commerce.
newsitem.headline: FTC member eyes privacy issues in online commerce.

text.p: Financial institutions that offer products and services electronically need to find ways to protect the privacy of their customers, a member of the Federal Trade Commission warned on Thursday.

"Privacy is a critical issue for consumers," FTC Commissioner Christine Varney told an industry group here. "Reliable safeguards for information privacy ... must be in place for electronic commerce to take off."
Varney expressed interest in the private development of technological solutions to privacy concerns.

"The private sector should be given the opportunity to lead," she said. "You can either lead, follow or get out of the way. Right now you've got an opportunity to lead and I think that window is probably closing."
Varney said she and several of her colleagues favor a self-regulatory approach to privacy issues stemming from electronic commerce.
"Self-regulation can work if (it is) pursued by industry with commitment and energy and backed up by strong government prosecution of fraud and deception," she said.
